full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin J.:- On an application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure this Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceeding of C.R Case No.218 of 2002, pending in the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Cognizance Court No.1, Moulvibazar Sadar, should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule is that the complainant filed C.R. Case No.218 of 2002 on 26.07.2000 in the Court of learned Magistrate, Class, Cognizance Court No.1, Moulvibazar, under Sections 364/34 of the Penal Code alleging inter alia that on 07.06.1999 at about 5.00 p.m. the accused’s named in the petition of complaint informed Mosonullah, victim of the case, that Settlement field Ammen was in the house of Arfanullah. With a bonafide belief the victim went to the house of Arfanullah. Thereafter the victim was missing. It is alleged that the accessed confined the victim in the house of Aifanullah for forcibly taking signature on some blank stamp papers. Being refused the accused’s confined him in an unknown place. The complainant made searching for the victim in different places, but in vain. It is the belief of the complainant that the accused’s in order to grab properties of the victim abducted him or killed him and hide his dead body. The complainant obtained Chairman Certificate from Gaznaipur Union Parishad to the effect that the victim Mosonullah was not died there. It is also stated that the delay was caused in collecting Chairman Certificate. 

 3. Upon receipt the petition of complain, the learned Magistrate sent the same to the Officer-in-Charge, Moulvibazar Police Station, for enquiry and report. After holding inquiry police submitted a report on 23.10.2000 stating that the complaint case is false and no occurrence took place on 07.06.1999 as alleged, since Mosonullah died a normal death before 22 years. 

 4. The complainant filed Naraji petition. The learned Magistrate sent the case for judicial inquiry to the teamed Magistrate, 3 Class, who after inquiry sent report on 14.05.2002 to the Court of Magistrate against 4 accused persons including the petitioners. The learned Magistrate of Cognizance Court No.1 by order dated 14.05.2002 took cognizance of the offence under Sections 364/34 of the Penal Code and issued summons against accused’s. However, the present petitioners surrendered before the Court of learned Magistrate and obtained bail on 13.11.2002. 

 5. Thereafter the accused petitioners preferred the instant Criminal Miscellaneous Case by filing an application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the present Rule and an order of stay. 

 6. Mr. Nirmatendu Dev, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners at the very outset submits that on the selfsame statements as alleged in the petition of complaint. Arabjan Bibi alias Abarjan Bibi wife of the victim also filed Petition Case No.428 of 1999 on 14.06.1999 in the Court of learned Magistrate, Class, Cognizance Court Nal, Moulvibazar, under Sections 364/34 of the Penal Code against the petitioners and 9 others as accuseds wherein present complainant was cited as witness No.1. The learned Magistrate, 1st Class, by order dated 14.06.1999 sent the complaint of Arabjan Bibi to the Officer-in-Charge, Moulvibazar Police Station, for taking action as per law and to inform the Court as to the action taken. The complainant Arabian Bibi remained absent in the Court on several dates and no inquiry report was received by the Court and ultimately the learned Magistrate by order dated 06.02.2000 filed the case in absence of the complainant. The learned Advocate also submits that from the statements of the petition of complaint, it is clear that the facts are preposterous and no case stands against the petitioners. He further submits that the proceeding is liable to be quashed as the allegation upon which it is based on the face of it is groundless or preposterous and no man of ordinary prudence will take any notice of it. He further submits that Section 561A is an independent inherent power of the High Court Division and this power can be exercised in case of the abuse of process of Court. He submits that Section 265C or 24IA of the Code of Criminal Procedure have nothing to do with quashing of a proceeding. He drew our notice to the annexures appended with supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners wherein three photocopies of the certified copy of the registered kabalas are annexed from where it appears that in registered kabala No.490 of 1979 dated 10.01.1979 Arabjan B ihi was the vendor wherein Arabjan Bibi's husband's name was written as late Mosonullah. In the same kabala the present complainant was also a vendor. In kabala No.493 of 1979 wherein also the name of the husband of Arabjan Bibi was written as late Mosonullah. In another kabala No.5119 of 1986 Md. Asadarullah was a vendor and herein also the name of the father of Asadarullah was mentioned as late Mosonullah. In this regard the learned Advocate submits that from the aforementioned kabalas, it is clear that the victim Mosonullah died long before 1979 which are tallied with the police reports. Lastly he submits that the learned Magistrate, 3rd Class, who inquired into the case as directed by the learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Cognizance Court No.1, Moulvibazar, violated the provisions of the provisio of Section 202(2A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and as such the same cannot be taken into consideration. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Latifa Akter and others -vs- the State and another, reported in 7 BLT(AD) 282; the case of Md. Shamsuddin alias Lambu and others -vs- the State and others, reported in 1988 BLD(AD) 93; the case of Habibur Rahman Mcllah (Ex-Member of Parliament, Dhaka-4) -vs-State and another, reported in 62 DLR(AD) 233 and the case of Faridul Alam -vs- State, reported in 61 DLR(AD) 93. 

 7. On the other hand Mr. Manjur Kader, learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the State submits that on inquiry the teamed Magistrate, 3rd Class, found a prima-facie case against the accused’s. By referring a decision he also submits where a prima facie case of criminal offence has been clearly made out, the High Court Division in a proceeding under Section 561A Cr. PC has little scope to scrutinize the truth or otherwise of any document or other evidence, which may be -used as a defence in a criminal proceeding. In support of his submission, the learned Assistant Attorney General referred to the case of Kamrul Islam (Md.) -vs-Atikuzzaman, reported in 49 DLR 258. 

 9. It appears that the complainant filed a petition of complaint before the learned Magistrate, Class, Cognizance Court No.1, Moulvibazar, on 26.07.2000 contending that on 07.06.1999 at 5.00 hours the accused’s informed the victim Mosonullah that Settlement Field Ameen is in the house of Arfanullah. With a bonafide belief the victim went there and thereafter he was missing. The date of occurrence was 07.06.1999 and the C.R. Case No.218 of 2002 filed on 26.07.2000, more than one year after the occurrence. In the statements of the case, it is stated that some of the witnesses saw that accused persons confined the victim in a house against his will and informed the incident to the complainant. Such a grave allegation came before the Court more than one year after the alleged occurrence. The cause for delay was shown that the complainant obtained certificate from the Chairman of Goznaipur Union that his brother was not died in the village under Goznaipur Union. Such a grave allegation was not informed to the local Police Station nor to the Chairman or Member of the Union Parishad. Delay in setting the law into motion by lodging of complaint in Court or of first information report at police station is normally viewed by courts with suspicion because there is possibility of concoction of evidence against an accused. So it becomes necessary for the prosecution to satisfactorily explain the delay. But when there is no explanation for the delay and when there is some explanation which is found to be not satisfactory, it casts a serious doubt and discredits the truthfulness of the prosecution version. The statement of C.R. Case No.218 of 2002 is hard to belief by a person with ordinary prudence. 

 10. When the learned Magistrate sent the case to the Police Station for inquiry and report, the inquiry Officer on inquiry found that Mosonullah died 22 years back in Kandigaon village. He also enquired wife, son and daughter of Mosonullah, against the Police report the complainant filed Naraji petition. On getting the same the learned Magistrate,  1st Class, Cognizance Court No.1, Moulvibazar sent it to the Magistrate, 3rd Class, Moulvibazar for inquiry who examined 4 witnesses including the complainant out of 8 witnesses cited in the C.R. Case. It is to be mentioned here that the allegations are under Sections 364/34 of the Penal Code which are triable by the Court of Sessions. The Magistrate inquired into the case under the provisions of Section 202(2A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Section 202(2A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure runs as follows: 

 "(2A) Any Magistrate inquiring into a case under this section may, if he thinks fit, take evidence of witnesses on oath; Provided that if it appears to the Magistrate that the offence complained of is triable exclusively by the Court of Sessions, he shall call upon the complainant to produce all his witnesses and examine them on oath." 

 Upon a close reading of proviso of Section 202(2A) it appears that the Magistrate who inquires into a case shall call upon the complainant to produce all his witnesses and examined them on oath. The provisions of the proviso is a mandatory one but in the present case the Magistrate who inquired into the case violates the provisions of the proviso of sub-section 2A of Section 202. Admittedly wife of the victim Arabjan Bibi filed Petition Case No.428 of 1999 under Sections 364/34 of the Penal Code in the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Moulvibazar on 14.06.1999 against the accused petitioners and others. That case also sent to the Moulvibazar Sadar Police Station for taking necessary action and to submit a report to the Court. That case was filed for non-appearance of the complainant Arabjan Bibi. In that case also the police submitted a report wherein it is clearly stated that Mosonullah died long before 1979. Apart from all the annexure as annexed in the application if we consider the allegations made in the C.R. Case, it is clear that those facts does not constitute an offence under Section 364 of the Penal Code. The petitioners came before this court at an initial stage. We like to quote a few lines from the judgment passed by our apex court in the case of Latifa Akter and others -vs-The State and another, reported in 7 BLT (AD) 282; our apex Court observed : 

 "Section 265C in Chapter XXII speaks of discharge of an accused in a trial before court of sessions. Section 241A in Chapter XX speaks of discharge of an accused in a trial by a magistrate. These are two independent Sections of the Code which deal with discharge of an accused brought to trial in respect of cases triable by a court of Sessions and by a court of Magistrate. These two Sections indicate that when an accused is brought for trial before a court of law the court upon hearing the parties and on consideration of the record of the case and the documents may discharge the accused. Theses two Sections have nothing to do with quashing of a proceeding, Section 561A is an independent inherent power of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court and this power can be exercised in case of abuse of process of court and for securing the ends of justice and or to give effect to any order under the code." 

 Under the facts and circumstances of case and for the reasons stated above in view of the cited decision, we are of the opinion that the C.R. Case No.218 of 2002 is a preposterous one and prolongation of the same would harass the innocent petitioners which is an abuse of the process of law. 

 12. The proceeding of C.R. Case No.218 of 2002 under Sections 364/34 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of the Magistrate, 1st Class, Cognizance Court No.1, Moulvibazar is quashed so far as it relates to the petitioners.
